text:
maria: Heads up — ASIA-1 GPU pools are showing slow provisioning and the runtime KV cache p95 has jumped. Observed during the 09:10 deploy. Errors and timeouts on warm starts.
ryan: seeing it, p95 token latency +220ms for short seqs. Any recent kernel/quant changes in the rollout? :thinking_face:
sam: I rolled the continuous-batcher change at 09:08 (small affinity tweak). Reverting now if it helps.
lee: infra-bot reported a scaling backlog: `hotpool_pending=142`. Some workers stuck in Pending due to pod init timeout.
maria: trying to divert traffic. Rolling a routing policy: set weight region=asia-1 -> 0.6, na-west -> 0.3, na1-fallback -> 0.1.
ryan: recommend 30% to na-west and enable graceful-fallback so requests hit na if kv misses escalate.
sam: reverting batcher affinity: `git revert 4a8b2c3` and `kubectl rollout restart ds/continuous-batcher -n asia-1`. Running now.
maria: infra-bot, open incident and tag oncall.
infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-2389 | Severity: S2 | Channels: #eng-infra #eng-oncall #incidents.
lee: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z ERROR runtime.kvcache lookup miss_latency_ms=120 p95_ms=340 batch_size=1 host=asia-1-rt-03
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z WARN  kubelet FailedMount: timeout waiting for volume mount for pod gpu-worker-7f4
```
ryan: for immediate mitigation enable request-level backpressure: set `BATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT=80` in asia-1 env and drop hotpool burst to avoid over-provisioning. That should reduce contention.
sam: applying env change via canary: `kubectl set env ds/continuous-batcher BATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT=80 -n asia-1 --record` then watch.
maria: I'm spinning up a small dedicated fallback pool in na-west with pinned models (quantized) to absorb high-rate short requests — cost tradeoff but keeps latency SLOs. Tagging finance for heads-up. :money_with_wings:
ops-handoff: FYI, allocating reserved GPUs to this pool will impact budget alerts — shifting 20% from spot to reserved could help stability.
lee: after revert + env change, I see pending hotpool drop to 28 in the last minute, p95 down to ~95ms. Still a few 503s during cold starts.
ryan: add quick KV prefix caching for common prompts so cold starts hit cache more often: flip `KVCACHE_PREFIX_ENABLED=true` for the canary.
maria: enabled prefix cache on canary, and set routing fallback threshold to 350ms. If latency >350ms requests route out of region.
sam: also noticed `oom_killer` on one gpu-worker; evicting noisy jobs helped. Added node toleration change to reduce bin-packing noise: `kubectl annotate node gpu-node-12 workload=noise=high`
infra-bot: Deployment event: continuous-batcher reverted by sam at 09:18Z.
lee: monitoring dashboards show cost per-token in asia-1 +18% since 09:00 due to emergency hotpool spin-up.
maria: acknowledge cost. Prioritizing user-facing latency > cost for now, will optimize after stabilization.
ryan: can we enable cross-region KV replication for hot prefixes as a follow-up? that should reduce cold miss rate. Filing a follow-up ticket.
ops-handoff: created ticket INF-3456 for cross-region replication and cost impact analysis.
maria: current status: revert applied, env canary + prefix cache enabled, traffic split to na-west in effect. p95 dropped to ~110ms and sustained. 503s trending down. Will monitor for 30m and then decide whether to failover more traffic.
sam: leaving a note: blocklist for noisy customers applied to limit aggressive small-sequence loops.
lee: should we run a controlled failover test later to validate rollback path?
maria: yes — schedule a verification window after this incident (T+2h).
maria: thanks everyone — will post an update in 15. :thumbsup:
